Built as a centre

Event Planners in Joondalup

Joondalup was designed rather than grown, so the venues, the hotels and the railway station sit inside one walkable centre. Hillarys adds sheltered marina water twenty minutes away. Both facts make guest logistics simpler than most of Perth. Describe the event once and planners covering the northern corridor will reply.

  • Thirty minutes to PerthThe Mitchell Freeway and the Joondalup line both run straight in.

The rarest thing on this coast is water that stays flat after three.

Most of Perth's coastline faces open ocean and takes the afternoon breeze head on. Hillarys is a built harbour, which is why an outdoor event there survives an hour that would end one at Trigg.

Joondalup is one of the few Australian cities that was drawn before it was built. The centre was designated, then filled in, which is why the civic buildings, the hotels, the shopping precinct and the railway station all sit within a few hundred metres of each other rather than sprawling along a highway. For anyone organising an event, that geometry is worth real money: guests can stay, arrive and leave without a car, and event planners in Joondalup routinely build a night around one walkable block.

The coast is the other half of the story. Hillarys, Sorrento, Mullaloo and Ocean Reef run north along the water, and Hillarys Boat Harbour is a constructed marina rather than an open beach, which makes it one of the few places near Perth where a late afternoon outdoor function is not at the mercy of the sea breeze. Yellagonga Regional Park and Lake Joondalup fill the eastern edge.

In and around Joondalup

What are you planning in Joondalup?

Six briefs cover most of the work here. What separates them is whether the event stays in the centre, where guests can walk between everything, or moves to the coast, where they cannot.

Start with

Weddings

Ceremony at Sorrento or Mullaloo, reception in a room with the water in it. The northern corridor does that combination well and the marina at Hillarys does it with shelter, which matters for a late afternoon in January. Guests can also stay in the centre and travel the twenty minutes across.

Find planners

Parties and milestones

Fiftieths and significant birthdays here usually happen at home in Duncraig, Kallaroo or Woodvale, where the blocks are generous and a marquee fits on the lawn. The planning work is catering out of a domestic kitchen, a hire delivery down a suburban street, and a finish time that keeps the neighbours onside.

Find planners

Corporate events

Edith Cowan University has its main campus in the centre, alongside the health and civic employers, so weekday work here runs to conferences, graduations, awards and training days. Accommodation inside walking distance is the local advantage, and it is why multi day programmes work better here than further north.

Find planners

Engagement parties

Sixty to a hundred people, early evening, somewhere with water in view. Hillarys and Ocean Reef take most of these because the marina holds its shape when the breeze arrives, and because there is parking, which is not true of every waterfront spot in Perth.

Find planners

Proposals

Burns Beach, the Sorrento foreshore and the paths through Yellagonga Regional Park are the settings people ask for here. All are public and all are busy at sunset, so the planning is about timing to the minute, an approach nobody notices, and a photographer already in position.

Private celebrations

Christenings, anniversaries, graduations and family reunions fill the smaller rooms through Joondalup, Currambine and Edgewater, usually under eighty guests and booked inside two months. That suits a coordinator taking over an existing plan for the final stretch rather than a full planning engagement.

Distance decides the level of help. An event inside the Joondalup centre is usually a coordination job, since everything sits within walking distance. Move it to a private property at Ocean Reef and the transport, hire and catering become separate problems.

Choosing well

Finding the right planner in Joondalup

Four questions are worth asking before you compare quotes. Two of them exist because this corridor runs a long way north, and suppliers price the far end differently to the near end.

No. 01

Ask where their supplier radius ends

Joondalup sits about 25 to 30 minutes from the Perth CBD on the freeway, which most metropolitan suppliers absorb without a travel charge. Keep going north past Currambine and Burns Beach and some start adding one. Ask a planner which of their regular caterers, hire companies and staffing crews already work this far north without a surcharge.

No. 02

Ask what the marina protects you from

Hillarys is a constructed harbour, so the water inside it stays workable when the open coast at Mullaloo or Sorrento is being blown out by the afternoon sea breeze. That difference is worth naming in the brief. Ask whether the space a planner proposes sits inside the breakwater or on the beach outside it, because the two behave nothing alike after three.

No. 03

Use the walkable centre deliberately

The Joondalup centre holds accommodation, the railway station, the civic buildings and the hospitality within a short walk, which is unusual for Perth. If half your guest list is coming from the city or interstate, ask a planner to build the night so nobody drives: a hotel block, a venue in the same precinct, and a walk instead of a coach.

No. 04

Check the university calendar against your date

Edith Cowan University's main campus is in the centre and it drives a weekday rhythm through the year, heaviest around graduation periods and orientation. That affects hotel availability and parking in the precinct more than it affects venues. Ask a planner to check accommodation before you lock a date if your guests need rooms nearby.

A built harbour is the only reliable way to keep an outdoor Perth function going past four in January.

On the ground

What a planned centre and a built harbour give you

Three things make event logistics here different from the rest of Perth: the centre was designed as a centre, the harbour is artificial, and the freeway and the rail line both run straight to the city.

Everything inside one walk

Joondalup was developed as a designated regional centre rather than growing out from an old town site, and the practical result is density in a place nobody expects it. Accommodation, the railway station, the civic and commercial buildings and the hospitality all sit inside a compact grid, so a guest can check in, walk to a function and walk back. That removes the two problems that dominate event planning across most of Perth: parking, and getting people home safely. If your guest list is travelling, this is the strongest argument for holding the event here rather than closer to the city.

The harbour is the weather plan

Hillarys Boat Harbour was built, not found. Breakwaters enclose it, which means the water and the air behind them stay usable when the open coast is unworkable. On a summer afternoon the sea breeze reaches Mullaloo, Sorrento and Ocean Reef with real force, and an outdoor setting on the beach side of the sand needs weighting and an early finish. Inside the harbour the same hour is manageable. It is a small distinction on a map and a large one on a run sheet, so establish which side of the wall your venue sits on before you sign.

Getting there, and the park behind it

Access from the city is genuinely straightforward, which is not true of every part of the northern corridor. Two routes run parallel, both roughly 25 to 30 minutes from the Perth CBD outside peak, which gives a planner two answers for guest transport rather than one.

  • Rail: the Joondalup line puts guests in the centre without a car.
  • Freeway: the Mitchell is fast outside peak and slower northbound on a weekday evening.
  • Yellagonga Regional Park and Lake Joondalup: bushland and water on the eastern edge, with public reserves that need council approval for anything set up.

Questions

Planning an event in Joondalup

What does an event planner cost in Joondalup?

Fees track the scope rather than the suburb. Easy Weddings, updated February 2026, puts on the day coordination at $1,500 to $2,000 and full service planning at $5,000 to $6,000 nationally, which is a reasonable starting point here. What tends not to appear on a Joondalup quote is a travel line, because the centre sits about 25 to 30 minutes from the Perth CBD and most metropolitan suppliers absorb that.

Is Hillarys a better bet than the beach for an outdoor event?

For a late afternoon in summer, yes. Hillarys Boat Harbour is a constructed marina with breakwaters around it, so the water stays flat and the air stays workable when the open coast at Sorrento or Mullaloo is taking the full sea breeze. A beach setting is still perfectly good in the morning or in the shoulder months. If your ceremony is at four in January, the harbour is the safer ground.

How do guests get to Joondalup from Perth?

By train or by freeway, and both take roughly 25 to 30 minutes outside peak. The Joondalup railway line runs into the centre, which means guests staying in the precinct do not need a car at all, and the Mitchell Freeway handles anyone driving. Northbound traffic on a weekday evening is the one thing to allow for, so a 6pm start needs a departure time on the invitation rather than a hopeful estimate.

Can we hold the ceremony and reception in the same precinct?

Often yes, and that is Joondalup's main advantage over the rest of the northern corridor. The centre was planned as a centre, so accommodation, hospitality and function space sit within a short walk of each other rather than a twenty minute drive. Ask a planner to build the whole night inside one block if your guests are travelling, because it removes both the coach cost and the question of how people get home.

Do we need a permit for a ceremony at Burns Beach or Yellagonga?

Yes, for anything you set up on public land, and beach reserves and the parklands around Lake Joondalup are exactly that. Expect a booking application, a fee, a cap on chairs and structures, a fixed time window and no exclusive use, which means the walking track stays open through your vows. Apply well ahead for a coastal reserve between October and March, and get a wet weather site approved at the same time.

When is accommodation hardest to get in the centre?

Around university graduation periods and through the December school holidays. Edith Cowan University has its main campus in the Joondalup centre and its calendar moves hotel demand in the precinct noticeably, while summer brings holiday traffic to the coast at Hillarys and Sorrento. If your guest list needs rooms within walking distance of the venue, book the accommodation before you confirm the date rather than after.
